card.name: Linking words before patient conditions
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as "with", "have" or "or" right after a patient group ("patients who", "adults with", "those with") and before a condition or difficulty, such as swallowing trouble, a feeding tube, a disability or renal problems.

modes.label: Patients who have / with
modes.description: The word after a patient group that introduces a condition or difficulty, often in administration instructions.
modes.example: For patients who<< have>> difficulty swallowing capsules, NEXIUM

modes.label: Adults with a condition
modes.description: "with" after adults or patients, leading into a disability or abnormal finding.
modes.example: Patients<< with>> abnormal renal function due to pre-renal

modes.label: Other list joiners
modes.description: Joining words or dashes between listed conditions, formats or dose units.
modes.example: NA for Adults with Schizophrenia<< or>> Schizoaffective Disorder Indication Init

card.writes: It suppresses Chinese medical words such as treatment, condition and patient, and it promotes no clear theme.
card.plain: It fires on the small word that links a patient group to their condition, as in "patients who have" or "adults with".
